topSignals.title: Bloom Energy shares jump ~9% on a Barclays upgrade plus a new carbon-capture fuel-cell venture with California Resources Corporation.
topSignals.text: Nov 3, 2026: Bloom (NYSE: BE) climbed about 9% intraday after an analyst price-target/rating upgrade from Barclays coincided with news of a new venture combining Bloom's fuel-cell technology with carbon capture, in partnership with California Resources Corporation (CRC) — a diversification signal beyond the AI-data-center backlog that has driven most of 2026's Bloom coverage. Shares Climb 9.1% Following Analyst Upgrade | Carbon-Capture Fuel-Cell Venture With California Resources

topSignals.title: Project Jupiter's community oversight structure takes its first formal steps — but the core fuel-cell deal terms, the Dec 7 air-permit hearing, and the El Paso Electric bond-breach dispute are all unchanged.
topSignals.text: The county-mandated community monitoring committee held its inaugural meeting (Oct 31/reported Nov 1), electing officers (Chair Lynn Moorer, Vice Chair Arturo Terrazas, Secretary Don Bassett) but setting no study topics yet; separately, Doña Ana County held a Nov 3 work session to begin shaping the $10M water/wastewater grant program tied to the project's economic-development agreement. Neither item touches the Dec 7 hearing date or the unresolved Oct 27 bond-breach notice. Committee inaugural meeting | Water-grant work session

items.text: Elcogen (priority): No new news-archive item since Sept 21, 2026 (Metrosert cooperation), confirmed via English- and German-language searches today — 44 days quiet. Status unchanged: elcoStack E3000 G2 platform (75% FC electrical efficiency / 90% with heat recovery, 33 kWh/kg H2 SOEC — vendor claims) in volume production at the 360 MW/yr ELCO I Tallinn factory.

Topsoe (priority): No new solid-oxide-specific release since the Aug 27, 2026 H1 2026 results/SOEC pathway reset, confirmed via English- and German-language searches today — 69 days quiet; topsoe.com/press-releases remains dominated by PTX/ammonia/SAF/blue-hydrogen news, out of SOFC/SOEC scope.

Today's checks — Tier 2 sweep plus dedicated rotation (new cycle, round 2: Sunfire, SolydEra) and Tier 3 rotation (cycle 6, round 4 — Denso, Thermax, completing this cycle), plus two Tier 3 sweeps (Reverion/Convion/Hexis/Doosan Fuel Cell/SK ecoplant/Weichai; Watt Fuel Cell/OxEon Energy/Nexceris/Kawasaki Heavy Industries/Miura/Fraunhofer IKTS): no new items for any company; all apparently-fresh hits (Elcogen's Tallinn factory launch, Sunfire's "€500M growth capital" story, SolydEra's Axiom Energy/GCEI North America tie-up) were confirmed via direct-date checks to be 2024/2025-vintage, not new.
Competitor roster: SOFC systems for data centers

Bloom Energy: Deployed/signed at multiple named sites — Oracle/Project Jupiter (NM, installation underway, Dec 7 air-permit hearing confirmed), AEP (1 GW), Brookfield EaaS, Nebius (328 MW/$2.6B, Vineland NJ), Equinix (>100 MW/19 sites), Aligned "Project Phoenix" (2 GW, PA), Hitachi (Japan), SK Eternix (Icheon/Paju, Korea, 28 MW, operational).

FuelCell Energy (incl. HyAxiom-branded products): Signed orders/PPAs — Fit Energy (up to 380 MW), Inuverse Korea (up to 100 MW), 75 MW Texas Capacity Reservation Agreement, SDCL (up to 450 MW). No named deployment live yet.

Doosan Fuel Cell/HyAxiom: Signed order — US AI data center supply contract (KRW 823.6B cumulative, mixed SOFC/PAFC); separately supplies SOFC stacks to Reverion. No named data-center site of its own yet.
Convion: Pipeline-only/pre-commercial under HD Hyundai ownership; no named data-center customer.
SK ecoplant: Pipeline-only (2023-vintage GDS Singapore SOFC deal); no new named data-center deployment.
Ceres Power's SOFC licensees (Doosan, Delta Electronics, Weichai): Licensing/pipeline-only; no named data-center deployment via Ceres licensing directly.
Reverion: Pipeline-only — Doosan-supplied SOFC stacks for rSOC power plants (Germany); no named data-center customer yet.
Petra Power: Pre-commercial, no named customer; first infrastructure deployment targeted 2028.

Bloom Energy (BE): Shares climbed ~9% on Nov 3 on a Barclays upgrade combined with a new carbon-capture fuel-cell venture announced with California Resources Corporation — see Top Signal #1. Shares Climb 9.1%

lcoe.text: Carry-forward, unchanged:* Virginia data-center electricity tax ($0.011/kWh); PJM Reliability Backstop ceiling (~$202.6/kW-year avoided-cost benchmark, filing suspended pending Feb 28, 2027 paper hearing); PJM's proposed 50 MW behind-the-meter netting threshold (pending FERC approval, 3-year grandfather); FCEL Torrington capex ($200-275M for 350-500 MW/yr by 2028); AEP/Bloom bundled utility-purchase benchmark ($2,944/kW capital+service); Germany's Netzpaket redispatch-curtailment risk (18-20% uncompensated annual-output exposure) for non-islanded SOFC deployments.

Pending calendar (updated):* Project Jupiter air-permit hearing Dec 7 (33 days out); Doña Ana County IRB "potential breach" notice over the El Paso Electric backup-power connection — unresolved; German Netzpaket/EEG 2027 Bundestag second/third reading targeted for the week of Nov 9-13 (5-9 days out), Bundesrat Nov 20 (16 days out); German KWK-Gesetz cabinet consideration remains undated past its Oct 14 target; FCEL lead-plaintiff deadline Nov 10 (6 days out); PJM backstop paper hearing runs to Feb 28, 2027; next EIA STEO Nov 10, 2026 (6 days out).
